transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I can’t slow down—I have too many important things to take care of and I feel driven to keep doing more, day and night. There is just so much that needs to be done for my work and my family, and I can't afford to stop.
Have you ever had a past episode of depression or another period like this when your mood and energy were unusually high? If so, when did that happen?
I don't recall ever having periods of depression or high energy like this in the past. I've usually just felt like my normal, calmer self before all of this started.

Before this current period, have you ever had a time lasting several days or longer when you felt very down or depressed, or another time when you were unusually energetic or euphoric like this? Even if it was milder, has anything like that ever happened before?

No, I really don't recall ever having times like that before. Before this all started, I just felt like my normal, calmer self and kept a pretty quiet routine. This is the first time I've ever felt this kind of intense drive or had any major mood shifts.

During this high-energy period, have you had experiences like hearing voices, seeing things others don’t, or being absolutely certain you have special powers or an unusually important mission? If yes, can you tell me briefly what that has been like?

Yes, I keep hearing a man's voice whispering right behind my ear, telling me not to sleep because everyone is counting on me. I'm also completely convinced that only I can prevent a disaster, because if I'm not watching every chart, the doctors and nurses will make fatal mistakes and my patients and parents will die. These experiences only started a couple of months ago when I got so revved up and stopped needing rest.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a first episode of markedly elevated/overactive state with decreased need for sleep, intense drive, and psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations and grandiose/paranoid delusional conviction of a special mission). There is no history of prior depressive, hypomanic, or manic episodes provided, supporting a current manic episode with psychotic symptoms rather than a recurrent bipolar diagnosis.
